description: LmdbBlockDb::get() always calls v.to_vec() on the LMDB-mapped slice, allocating a Vec on every read. LMDB provides zero-copy reads: the data pointer is valid for the lifetime of the read transaction. For a block store that serves many concurrent readers (e.g. article body serving), callers that only need to hash or stream the bytes cannot avoid the allocation. Exposing a get_with callback API or a type that holds the rtxn alive alongside the slice would enable zero-copy access. Impact: each article body read allocates a Vec equal to the block size (up to tens of KB).
title: lmdb: get() copies value bytes to Vec on every read; zero-copy path not exposed
